final_message:
Fixed. In your repro, `Test` now resolves to `{ prop1: "hello"; }`.

**Cause.** The type printer in 5.7 reuses the type node from a property's declaration when it can. For `prop1: stringWrapper() as Wrapper<"hello">` it reused the `Wrapper<"hello">` from the `as` without checking it against the property's actual type. That is the right type for the property on the object literal. It is the wrong one for the same property on a mapped or instantiated type. Here `Unwrap` maps `prop1` to `"hello"`, but the printer still showed `Wrapper<"hello">`. Your separate-line workaround avoided this because that declaration has no inline assertion in a property.

The wrong text also showed up in declaration emit. For example, `function mk<T>(x: T) { return { v: [] as T[] } }` called as `mk("a")` printed `{ v: T[] }` instead of `{ v: string[] }`.

**Fix.**
- **`typeFromPropertyAssignment`** in `src/compiler/expressionToTypeNode.ts` now reuses the assertion's type node only if it matches the symbol's type. It uses the same check already applied to explicit type annotations (`canReuseTypeNodeAnnotation`). Otherwise it prints the symbol's real type.
- **Class properties with initializers** had the same problem. Mapping over `class C { p = x as Foo<"a">; q = 1 }` printed the unmapped initializer types. I added a small `isSymbolOfDeclaration` method to the checker's resolver (`src/compiler/checker.ts`, `src/compiler/types.ts`). `typeFromProperty` now uses the initializer only for the property the declaration itself declares, not for one derived from it.

**Test.** I added `tests/cases/compiler/typeAssertionInPropertyOfMappedType.ts` with accepted baselines. It covers your repro, a mapped function return (checked through its `.d.ts`), a generic function returning an object with assertions, and a mapped class. I confirmed your repro produced the wrong output before the change.

I ran the compiler, conformance, fourslash, fourslash-server and project test runners and they all pass, with no changes to existing baselines. I did not run the full suite as one run, because it ran out of memory on this machine, so I ran the runners separately. ESLint is clean on `expressionToTypeNode.ts`. I did not lint `checker.ts` or `types.ts`. The dprint formatter couldn't download its plugins in the sandbox, so I haven't run it.
